목표: 이 프로젝트(`c:\Users\edn_y\renew_nineonelabs`)의 Claude/AI 가이드 문서들이 Claude Code 공식 best practices의 7개 핵심 영역을 얼마나 다루고 있는지 매핑한 감사 리포트를 만들어 줘.

검사 대상 문서 (모두 읽어 한 번에 평가):
- `CLAUDE.md`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `BRAND.md`
- `README.md`
- `.claude/rules/frontend.md`
- `.claude/rules/php.md`
- `.claude/rules/scss.md`
- `.claude/BEST_PRACTICES.md`
- `.claude/SETUP_CHECKLIST.md` (untracked)
- `.claude/skills/*` 와 `.claude/agents/*` 가 있다면 목록만 (메타데이터)
- `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json` (hook/permission 설정 — 문서 자체는 아니지만 "권한·hook 자동화"가 코드/설정에 이미 반영되었는지 판단할 근거)
- `.codex/config.toml`, `.codex/rules/default.rules`

평가할 7개 영역 (각각 "있음/부분/없음" + 근거 파일·라인 + 짧은 인용):
1. **도구 연동 및 권한 설정** — MCP, gh CLI, allowedTools, /permissions, sandboxing, hooks 자동화 관련 가이드
2. **적극적인 개입 및 수정 (course-correct)** — Esc/Esc, /rewind, /clear, "두 번 이상 같은 실수 시 컨텍스트 리셋" 같은 워크플로 가이드
3. **컨텍스트 관리 (context hygiene)** — /clear, /compact, 큰 출력은 chop/agent로 격리, 불필요 파일 안 읽기 등
4. **반복 작업 자동화** — non-interactive `claude -p`, hooks (예: tsc 자동 실행), pre-commit, fan-out 스크립트
5. **병렬 처리** — 다중 Claude 세션, agent teams, writer/reviewer 패턴, 서브에이전트 병렬 호출
6. **TDD (테스트 주도 개발)** — Vitest 사용, 테스트 우선 작성, 검증 기준 (verification criteria) 강조
7. **플랜모드 / Explore→Plan→Implement→Commit** — Plan Mode 사용 권장, /init, 큰 변경 시 plan 우선 등

각 영역마다 다음 형식으로 결과:

```
### 1. 도구 연동 및 권한 설정 — [있음 | 부분 | 없음]
- 근거: AGENTS.md:42 "..."
- 빠진 부분: ...
- 추천 추가 위치: AGENTS.md > 새 섹션 "Permissions & Hooks", 또는 .claude/BEST_PRACTICES.md 새 Part
```

마지막에 "총평 한 줄 + 보강 우선순위 Top 3" 만 적어줘. 600단어 이내로 요약.

주의:
- 코드는 수정하지 마. 읽기만.
- BRAND.md/brand/* 파일은 브랜드 카피이므로 best-practices 평가 대상 아님 — 명시적으로 "out of scope"로 표시.
- chop은 이미 rtk 로 교체됐다는 점을 인지 (memory MEMORY.md 11번 라인 참고).

19

21	- Dev server: `http://localhost:8888`

24	- Prefer `rtk` for output that may exceed a few lines (git, search, typecheck, docker, PowerShell pipelines). Examples: `rtk git status`, `rtk git diff`, `rtk git log --oneline -20`, `rtk grep ...`, `rtk docker compose ps`. Short one-liners may skip `rtk`. In WSL Remote sessions the PreToolUse hook auto-rewrites `git`/`docker`/`tsc`/etc. to their `rtk`-prefixed equivalents.
25	- Windows PowerShell: explicit UTF-8 for Korean text reads/writes.
26	
27	## Architecture
28	
29	- Public routes are closure-based in `routes/web.php` and render via `render()`. Do not reintroduce Barba.js or SPA navigation contracts.
30	- Ownership separation: do not duplicate work in `AppManager`, `PageRuntime`, or `PageTheatreBinder`. See `.claude/BEST_PRACTICES.md` Part A and memory `project_ts_map.md` for boundaries.
31	- Page scenes: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`. Theatre bindings: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`. Page-scoped runtime: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/runtime/`. Shared types: `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`. Keep shared engine/runtime code out of page folders.
32	- Image uploads: entry point `imageUpload()` in `inc/lib/func.php`. Auto-creates `.webp` sibling via `\Core\ImageProcessor::makeWebpSibling()`. DB stores the original filename. New upload paths that bypass `imageUpload()` must call `makeWebpSibling()` after `move_uploaded_file()`. Detail in `.claude/rules/php.md`.
33	- `Core\ImageProcessor` (`src/Core/ImageProcessor.php`): WEBP via spatie/image 1.10.6 (GD). jpg/jpeg/png/gif covered; svg/ico skipped. Resize threshold 2560px. Quality 82.
34	
35	## Editing Rules
36	
37	- Follow existing custom MVC patterns; no Laravel/Symfony conventions.
38	- SCSS: BEM naming. Use shared `fluid(min, max)` over raw responsive values. `var(--token, fallback)` is forbidden — use `var(--token)` or `fluid(...)` directly. Full SCSS rules in `.claude/rules/scss.md`.
39	- TypeScript/Three.js: dispose every geometry/material/texture; no object creation in render loops; match `addEventListener` with `removeEventListener`. Full rules in `.claude/rules/frontend.md`.
40	- PHP: closure routing, `nb_` table prefix, migrations only for schema changes. Full rules in `.claude/rules/php.md`.

49	- Never use npm build/watch/install for verification — saved files are already handled by Vite.

110	## 4. OOP / SOLID checklist for new code
111	
112	Run through this list mentally before writing the class.
113	
114	### SRP — Single Responsibility
115	- One "reason to change" per class. If you need "and" to describe it, split.
116	- If > 400 lines, ask whether 2+ smaller classes fit better.
117	- **New code must not be added to `AppManager` or `ContactWizard`.** Extend in a sibling class.
118	
119	### OCP — Open/Closed
120	- New page variants → add to factory map (`PageTheatreBinder.PAGE_THEATRE_ADAPTER_FACTORIES`), never a new `if (pageId === ...)` branch.
121	- New light/object types → register in a creator map (`SceneLights._creators` pattern), never a switch.
122	- Use the `ObjectFactoryRegistry` for new scene-object kinds.
123	
124	### LSP — Liskov Substitution
125	- Subclasses of `SceneObject` must respect the contract: `init` → `runObject` → `runUpdate` → `dispose`, no partial cycles.
126	- `override` keyword is mandatory on overridden methods.
127	
128	### ISP — Interface Segregation
129	- Adapter interfaces are split by capability (`PageTheatreBootAdapter`, `PageTheatrePreviewAdapter`, `PageTheatreIntroAdapter`, `PageTheatreIntroActionAdapter`, `PageTheatreSceneSyncAdapter`).
130	- Implement only the capabilities you need; the composite `PageTheatreAdapter` is optional-by-field.
131	- Do not add fields to existing interfaces just to avoid a type check — add a narrower interface.
132	
133	### DIP — Dependency Inversion
134	- `Engine` accepts `EngineDependencies` (`sceneFactory`, `modelLoaderFactory`). Use this for testing/swapping.
135	- High-level modules must not `new ConcreteClass()` mid-constructor when a factory slot exists.
136	- Cross-class lookup goes through `context.getObject(id)` (O(1)), never `scene.getObjectByName(...)` (O(n)).
137	
138	### Disposal symmetry
139	Every class that allocates is responsible for releasing:
140	
141	| Creates | Must release in `dispose()` |
142	|---|---|
143	| `addEventListener` | `removeEventListener` with same reference + options |
144	| `setTimeout` / `setInterval` | `clearTimeout` / `clearInterval` |
145	| `requestAnimationFrame` | `cancelAnimationFrame` |
146	| `new MutationObserver` / Intersection / Resize | `.disconnect()` |
147	| `THREE.BufferGeometry` | `.dispose()` |
148	| `THREE.Material` | `.dispose()` + all texture slots |
149	| `THREE.Texture` | `.dispose()` — or register via `SceneObject._ownedTextures` |
150	| `THREE.Light` | `.parent?.remove(light)` + `light.dispose?.()` + target removal |
151	| `Element.animate()` | `.cancel()` |
152	| Debounce / scheduler | `.offCancel()` |
153	| Theatre subscription | Call returned unsubscribe |
154	| Scene pub/sub subscription | Call returned unsubscribe |
155	
156	Use the helpers:
157	- `utils/disposeObject3D.ts` — traverses an Object3D, disposes geometries + materials (with all 21 texture slots + shader uniform textures).
158	- `utils/disposeObject3D.ts#removeAndDispose(node)` — detach from parent and dispose.
159	
160	### Side effects
161	- Constructors: wiring only. No DOM queries, no RAF, no fetches, no listener registration. Do it in `init()`/`mount()`.
162	- Module top-level: no side effects. No `window.addEventListener` at import time. No singletons created at import time.
163	- Static fields: no mutable state. If you need tracking (e.g., `ContactWizard._instances`), it must be reset by a static `dispose()`.

165	## 5. THREE.js GPU/CPU optimization playbook
166	
167	### Render-loop hot path rules (hard bans)
168	
169	1. **No `new Vector2/Vector3/Matrix4/Quaternion/Euler` inside `runUpdate`, `render`, or any per-frame callback.**
170	   - Use module-scope or instance `_scratch` fields. Mutate with `.copy()`, `.set()`, `.applyMatrix4()`.
171	2. **No object literals inside per-frame paths.**
172	   - Cache resolved options in an instance scratch object. Recompute only when inputs change (in `setOptions`, not in `runUpdate`).
173	3. **No `scene.getObjectByName()` per frame.** Use `context.getObject(id)` (O(1) Map lookup) or subscribe via `Scene.onObjectRegistered`.
174	4. **No `new Set()` / `Object.keys()` / `Array.from()` inside hot path.** Pre-compute key arrays when source changes.
175	5. **No `.getSnapshot()` called more than once per frame.** Cache locally in the function.
176	6. **No `uniform.tX.value = texture` per frame.** Textures set once at material creation; only scalars/vectors update per frame.
177	
178	### World matrix freshness
179	
180	- Before reading `object.matrixWorld` or `object.getWorldPosition()`, call `object.updateWorldMatrix(true, false)` if the render hasn't run yet this frame.
181	- Known call sites that already do this: `Engine._resolveFollowAnchor`, `CameraTargetRuntime.resolveFollowAnchor`, `CloudPlane._applyRocketUniforms`.
182	
183	### GPU memory
184	
185	- Every cached model must be cloned with independent materials. `ModelLoader.loadGLTF` handles this via `_cloneMaterialsInPlace` — don't bypass.
186	- Shader swaps on cached meshes must guard against re-application. Use `userData.__<name>Applied` tag (see `Ground._applyGroundShader`).
187	- On page teardown: `Engine.dispose()` → `Scene.dispose()` → every `SceneObject.dispose()` → `disposeObject3D(timelineRoot)`.
188	- Secondary renderers (like `WorksSceneManager`): must call `renderer.dispose()` AND `renderer.forceContextLoss()`.
189	
190	### Materials / shaders
191	
192	- Clone materials before mutation to avoid cache pollution: `material.clone()`.
193	- `onBeforeCompile` closures must not retain frame-local state. Store uniform refs in `userData.shader` for later mutation.
194	- `needsUpdate = true` is set exactly once (after `onBeforeCompile` assignment). Never in the render loop.
195	
196	### Post-processing
197	
198	- `EffectComposer.setSize(w, h)` receives CSS pixels (composer applies pixel ratio internally).
199	- `UnrealBloomPass.resolution.set(w, h)` receives CSS pixels (matches composer).
200	- Do not call `renderer.setSize()` inside the render loop. Use a resize listener → `ResponsiveRuntime` dispatch.
201	
202	### Profiling
203	
204	- Chrome DevTools Performance → look for frames > 16.67ms and GC sawteeth.
205	- `chrome://tracing` / WebGL Inspector for draw-call counts.
206	- Self-check: 60fps with GC events < 2/sec. Allocation profiler should show ~0 new Vector2/Vector3/Object per frame.

208	## 6. Responsive architecture
209	
210	The project centralizes all responsive state through `ResponsiveRuntime` (pub/sub). Build new responsive features on top of it; do not add ad-hoc `window.matchMedia` listeners.
211	
212	### Contract
213	
214	```ts
215	const runtime = ResponsiveRuntime.getDefault();
216	const snapshot = runtime.getSnapshot();
217	// snapshot.breakpoint: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
218	// snapshot.viewportWidth / viewportHeight
219	// snapshot.render.clampedPixelRatio
220	// snapshot.device.isMobile
221	// snapshot.reducedMotion
222	// snapshot.performance tier
223	
224	const unsubscribe = runtime.subscribe((next) => {
225	  // react to breakpoint / viewport / reduced motion changes
226	});
227	// In dispose(): unsubscribe();
228	```
229	
230	### Extension rules
231	
232	- **New responsive value:** derive from `snapshot` inside the consumer. Don't add fields to `ResponsiveSnapshot` unless multiple consumers need it.
233	- **Config with breakpoint variance:** use `utils/ResponsiveValue.ts` (`{ sm, md, lg, xl, default }`) — declare in `config/`, resolve at call site.
234	- **Reduced motion:** check `snapshot.reducedMotion` and provide a degraded path (no infinite loops, no parallax). Required for accessibility.
235	- **Pixel ratio / performance tier:** read `snapshot.render.clampedPixelRatio` and `snapshot.performance` — used by `Engine` and `PostProcessor` automatically. Pass the snapshot through, don't re-derive.
236	- **Orientation / mobile only:** prefer `snapshot.device.isMobile` over UA sniffing.
237	- **Three.js resizing:** single path. Resize listener → `ResponsiveRuntime.updateFromWindow()` → subscribers (`Engine.applyResponsiveSnapshot`, `PostProcessor.resize`, `WorksSceneManager`). Do not bind `window.resize` in new code.
238	
239	### CSS integration
240	
241	- `ResponsiveRuntime._applyCssVariables(snapshot)` publishes CSS custom properties. Read them in SCSS via `var(--vw, 1vw)` etc., not through JS-computed inline styles.
242	
243	### Touch vs hover
244	
245	- Hover UX (`mouseenter` / `mouseleave`) stays on `MouseEvent` semantics — it's desktop-only by design.
246	- Drag / press / click target → `PointerEvent` (`pointerdown` / `pointerup` / `pointermove`) with `pointerId` tracking. See `CustomCursor` and `WorksPageRuntime` patterns.
247
